workloads.scope: Validate fixed-input binary bitwise AND, OR, and XOR across signed and unsigned i8/u8/i16/u16/i32/u32/i64/u64 and the current x86-64 Int/UInt aliases, plus exact i8-to-i32 and u8-to-i16 widening before OR, with exact twelve-line decimal output. C23 and Rust 2024 retain runtime operands; W uses fixed literal inputs, so runtime-equivalent ranking is deferred.

Validate checked ordinary arithmetic-right and non-overflowing left shifts across signed and unsigned i8/i16/i32/i64 and the current x86-64 Int/UInt aliases, plus masked left/right and logical right policies across signed and unsigned i8/u8 through i64/u64. Cover masked counts at width and width+1, logical counts at zero and width-1, and the u64 small-value edges. The bounded native route does not yet execute this combined W witness. C23 and Rust retain runtime inputs while individual W operations may fold literals; performance ranking is deferred until the W route executes equivalent runtime work.
Execute checked signed and unsigned 64-bit integer power with UInt exponents, right association, and exact output.
Execute prefix and checked power composition with power-before-left-prefix precedence, prefixed bases, right association, and exact output.
Execute all eleven checked scalar compound assignments on one mutable local and preserve exact SSA result output.

Validate strict binary32 and binary64 arithmetic, comparisons, signed zero, and NaN output with exact output. W artifacts are compile-time-folded semantic/output witnesses, not equivalent runtime-float work; C and Rust retain runtime operations as references.

Validate f32.fromBits(u32)/toBits() and f64.fromBits(u64)/toBits() round trips for negative zero, positive infinity, and one quiet-NaN payload per width, printing exact unsigned decimal bit patterns. W's literal inputs and C23/Rust runtime inputs are correctness-only until equivalent runtime work is established.

Validate successful fixed-input checked +, -, *, /, %, +=, -=, *=, /=, and %= across signed and unsigned i8/i16/i32/i64 and the current x86-64 Int/UInt aliases with exact output. Fault behavior is covered by the W run gates only; C23 and Rust are correctness references for the successful domain.

Validate fixed-input signed unary negation and bitwise complement over i8/i16/i32/i64 and Int plus unsigned complement over u8/u16/u32/u64 and UInt, alongside literal prefix negation. W may fold literal call arguments while C23 and Rust preserve runtime operands, so performance ranking is deferred until runtime-equivalent W work exists.

Validate fixed-input signed and unsigned i8/i16/i32/i64 plus Int/UInt wrapping-policy representatives for add, subtract, multiply, negate, power, and left shift with exact five-line decimal output. Performance ranking is deferred until W preserves equivalent runtime work.

Validate representative fixed-width and x86-64 Int implicit integer widenings across return, call argument, local binding, and unsigned-to-signed cases with exact output. Performance ranking is deferred until W preserves equivalent runtime work.

Validate exact implicit integer-to-float and f32-to-f64 widening across return, call argument, local binding, mixed arithmetic, and mixed comparison contexts with exact output. W currently folds the witness while C and Rust retain runtime inputs, so no performance ranking is claimed.

Validate explicit integer truncating-bits conversions across signed and unsigned 8/16/64-bit values, including narrowing, widening, signedness changes, and x86-64 Int/UInt aliases, with exact decimal output. Performance ranking is deferred until W preserves equivalent runtime work.

The public witness exercises all four signedness quadrants with representative i16/u16-to-i8/u8 conversions plus the x86-64 UInt-to-Int alias path, covering low, in-range, and high values where source domains permit and clamping UInt::MAX. The focused compiler matrix remains the proof for all 100 source/destination pairs across the ten integer spellings and scalar 8/16/32/64-bit boundaries. These compact C23 and Rust 2024 correctness references do not establish comparable production runtime work, so ranking remains deferred.

Validate fixed-input signed and unsigned comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) across i8/u8/i16/u16/i32/u32/i64/u64 and the current x86-64 Int/UInt aliases, plus a u8-to-i16 comparison after argument widening, with exact output. Performance ranking is deferred until W preserves equivalent runtime work.

Convert the runtime-derived user argument count from logical usize to i8 exactly, evaluate checked +, -, *, /, and % over that runtime value, and publish output only after success. NumericConversionError remains a typed outcome mapped to status 1; arithmetic overflow remains a distinct panic/fault outcome mapped to status 2. Both paths run reverse-order owner cleanup and root finalization before host adaptation, and neither publishes buffered output. This bounded process witness does not replace the focused all-pairs compiler matrix or establish a general panic runtime.

This catalog witness covers only the success result (empty stdout/stderr), is correctness-only, and does not represent the separate failure gate as a benchmark case.

sampling.zeroCpuDisclosure: Production runtime CPU originates in Windows 100 ns Job Object counters and is normalized with floor rounding to catalog microseconds; compile-side Bun counters are already microseconds. Zero-valued samples remain valid.

resultContract.artifact: Artifact digest and sizeBytes are correctness-build facts, not repeated samples. Windows results may carry validated PE layout metadata; native Linux and Linux/WSL results may carry validated ELF64 layout metadata. Historical records without layout metadata are not measured.
resultContract.storage: Full-fidelity local results stay under ignored benchmarks/results and are consumed after a successful update; raw samples are never copied into Git.
resultContract.runtimeMeasurement: run is the complete target-process invocation measured by one native helper batch per warmup/raw series; the target process is fresh per sample, while helper, WSL startup, and DrvFS staging are outside each production sample.

bestMetricsContract.storage: Only the current lower-is-better value for each comparable category and metric is stored in this catalog.
bestMetricsContract.rule: Update compares only lower-is-better positive values inside one exact workload, source-equivalence, platform, artifact target, ABI, profile, host, recipe class and policy category; toolchain and recipe may improve that same cell, while correctness outputs never rank. When a new runner kernel publishes one live lane, evidence from older runner digests in that lane is removed rather than retained as repository history. Artifact layout metadata is emitted only on the artifact-size cell; an equal-size validated candidate with the same equivalence, source and recipe evidence may replace a metadata-less winner as a complete provenance update, while different cells or evidence are never merged. The linux-wsl-x64 lane is retained for same-host regression and same-physical-hardware diagnostics only; its WSL platform evidence is required and it is never native-Linux or cross-host ranking evidence.
